claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding provide protection under normal subcritical-water conditions.
Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding undergo premature failure in high-temperature steam.
High-temperature failure of the Cr coating is caused by Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
An ultra-thin W interlayer placed at the Cr/zirconium-alloy interface will limit Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Limiting Cr-Zr interdiffusion with a W interlayer will improve coating durability in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
The proposed W interlayer has a thickness on the order of tens of nanometers.
The W interlayer will act as a stable refractory diffusion barrier between Cr and the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Tungsten has a high melting point.
Tungsten has sufficiently low diffusivity to inhibit Cr and Zr transport across the coating/substrate interface.
Inhibiting Cr-Zr interdiffusion will prevent the formation of detrimental Cr-Zr intermetallic phases during high-temperature exposure.
Preventing Cr-Zr intermetallic formation will maintain the integrity of the Cr coating.
Preventing Cr-Zr intermetallic formation will maintain the protective properties of the Cr coating.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the W interlayer will reduce interfacial diffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the W interlayer will produce a more stable coating microstructure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the W interlayer will improve oxidation resistance during prolonged normal operation.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the W interlayer will improve oxidation resistance during transient high-temperature steam exposure.

The proposed intervention is applicable from approximately 300-400 degrees Celsius up to approximately 1200 degrees Celsius, for exposures ranging from hundreds of hours to about one hour at the highest temperature.
The long-term stability of the W interlayer under neutron irradiation and its effect on coating-substrate bonding remain unverified.
